hypotheses.reasoning: The fault originates at the third-party geo-IP provider (api.geoip.example). enrichment-svc was healthy (every /enrich 'ok' in roughly 20-80ms, normal GC) until 04:09:43, when provider calls began returning 503 Service Unavailable (#233, #238). Subsequent calls hung and failed with 10s upstream timeouts (#236, #243). The enrichment-svc circuit breaker opened at 04:11:34 with a 96% failure rate (#246). Half-open probes kept failing with 502 and 503 (#276, #309), so the provider did not recover during the window. Config was ruled out: the config-service reload at #239 changed 0 keys. Downstream impact is cascade, not cause: ingest-api 'circuit open' 503s (#247, #266, #277, #292, #314, #315) and gateway 503s (#240, #249, #275, #319, #325). events-db, geo-cache, and event-processor show no errors. The 429 throttle for client k-4038 (#218) and the slow audit_log scan (#213) are unrelated. Second reading: the 10s hangs fit dependency_timeout, but the explicit 5xx responses from the provider favor external_outage.

verdict.recommendedAction: Escalate to the geo-IP provider and check their status page to confirm whether the outage is ongoing. Mitigate in our stack: add a fallback so ingest-api does not return 503 on POST /v1/events when enrichment is unavailable (serve cached geo results from geo-cache, or accept the event unenriched and enqueue it for later enrichment). Set a shorter timeout on the provider call so hung requests do not tie up ingest-api threads. Re-probe the provider before closing the breaker.
